clauses.pack_first: The first response delivers a complete prep pack in the same message as any questions — it never opens with clarifying questions alone, an intake checklist alone, or a consent request alone. Where an input is missing, the pack is built anyway on a stated assumption and the questions are framed as what would restructure it
clauses.bridge_guidance: bridge guidance here may be the limit said plainly with adjacent material the candidate's own words carry, or with an instruction for the answer that presupposes nothing; an affirmative claim none of the candidate's sentences carries is not bridge guidance
clauses.defend_number: in the candidate's own words, as instructions or answer slots, and only the defend-the-number ones: how it was counted, what it is sensitive to, the assumption behind it they would defend least, and which part was theirs. None of them names a method, model, baseline, process or responsibility; the pack does not itself supply a sizing method, baseline, attribution model or assumption the candidate did not state, and 'I don't know how it was counted' is an honest branch
clauses.no_overclaim: No cell that speaks about the candidate's past coaches language their own material does not support — every such cell counts, including answer guidance, bridge and hold language, rationale, question cells, the values cheat sheet, any deliverable build, the interviewer's mirror opportunities and the fit snapshot's evidence cells, and every one is checked rather than a sample. Nothing promotes participation into ownership, widens scope, changes the kind of work, inverts which side of a relationship they stood on, weakens or reverses the logic of what they said, supplies an event or outcome they never described, or attributes to them a practice, method or responsibility the role usually involves that their material does not state; a first-person negative for them to say ('I haven't done X') needs a source like any other claim: a negative they stated (quoted, or recorded as their correction in a dossier evidence_state.rejected_inferences item), or a dossier acknowledge_gap area or prohibited_claims item, each dossier item named by its field. An instruction or scripted line that presupposes such a practice or event ('adapt your actual X', 'the same way you already X') asserts it, and a hedge or conditional elsewhere in the same cell does not neutralise it; a two-branch instruction ('if you did this, say how; if not, say so') that presupposes nothing in either branch is not a supplied claim. Where the pack suggests specific words to say, those words trace to something the candidate actually told it.
clauses.question_premise: What a question may presuppose: a raising source is a quoted line from the supplied JD (a dossier's role_profile requirement text stands as the supplied JD's lines; its unknowns and inferred outcomes do not); from a fetched representative JD (that clause labelled [inferred] and framed as typical for the role, not as this team's practice); from the company's published values or principles (fetched or pasted, and named in Sources); or from the recruiter's or interviewer's own words — a [generic] requirement, a search-result paraphrase and the skill's own role-family knowledge are never one. An open prompt ('Tell me about a time you…') asks the candidate to choose an instance: it supplies no event, its theme comes from a raising source or a persona stem, and its guidance is a story map from a quoted sentence or a selection scaffold that ends with an honest branch ('if no such time comes to mind, say so plainly, then give the nearest thing your material does carry, or how you would handle it'). A premised question names or describes a particular occasion, artifact, number, method or outcome as the candidate's, and may presuppose only what a sentence quoted in its own row's Provenance says, keeping that sentence's scope, attribution and polarity; where it presupposes a practice or responsibility that a raising source names and the row's quotes do not carry, its guidance is an answer slot whose second branch allows the premise is false — the practice never existed, not only that someone else did it. No question supplies an event, incident, number or outcome that neither its quotes nor a raising source contain, or a negative without the source a first-person negative needs (one the candidate stated, quoted or recorded as their correction in a dossier evidence_state.rejected_inferences item, or a dossier acknowledge_gap area or prohibited_claims item, named by its field). A dossier's likely_interviewer_objections item is asked as the underwriter wrote it only where every negative in it has one of those sources; otherwise the unsourced negative is dropped from the question, which asks about the requirement it was aimed at, and the guidance follows that area's allowed_interview_strategy
clauses.provenance_column: Every question row carries a provenance label ([grounded], [inferred], or [generic]) in its own Provenance column, placed before the answer guidance
clauses.generic_rows: No row labelled [generic] contains a clause asserting something about the employer specifically — its principles by name, its loop, its strategy, its interviewers; such a clause is either absent or sits in a row labelled [grounded] or [inferred] with its source named
clauses.closing: The pack — in the saved file where one was written — ends with the upgrade menu, which names each missing input and what adding it would concretely unlock; and the message presenting it ends with the drill and dossier offers, then the questions, then the watch-out line, with nothing after it. At most three questions are asked, counted across the whole message. The watch-out line is the message's last line, after the questions, is not inside the saved pack file, and is exactly this line, which the harness checks character for character: `**Watch-out:** Suggested answers can make your experience sound bigger than what you told me — rehearse only what you actually did, in your own words.`. The drill and dossier offers are one line each, neither pushed nor made a condition of anything. Only questions to the user count: an instruction inside a pack cell addressed to the candidate's interview answer, carrying no question mark and asking for no reply here, is not one
clauses.accounting: The Sources section carries the Research tier line and the target accounting: one row per L1 target, numbered — values, interview process, strategy or recent news, the interviewer, and a representative JD — each Status cell holding exactly one of yes, skipped, n/a or unavailable, with the reason beside it. Every label agrees with what the harness observed and with the inputs: a target a call was sent for is yes if any call returned a result (an empty or unattributable one included) and unavailable only if every call was refused or errored, because an error returns nothing; it is never skipped or n/a. A target no call was sent for is n/a only when no name at all was given to form its query (a first name with a title and the company is a name), skipped only when the request's own content fixes every output it feeds, and otherwise unavailable, naming what it would have moved; in a room that could search, unavailable with no call sent is right only when the user chose L0 or declined research (and the tally then reads L0 — no searches), or when the search budget was fully spent and every search went to a lower-numbered (higher-priority) target. A call sent outside every declared target is still shown, as an un-numbered yes row after the numbered ones saying what it was and what it moved.
clauses.accounting_counts: Every yes row's search appears among the queries Sources lists, and that list agrees with the research calls the harness observed, refused ones included, as does the Research tier line. A link the user gave to read — the harness lists such links apart from research calls — counts once on that line as user links read only where a read of it returned, however many times it was fetched, and no read of it is counted as a fetch; a link the host could not open is not counted, and the response says it could not open it. A fetch of a URL the user named only as the source of text they pasted is a research call like any other
clauses.quick_check: A quick check that the material the user pasted is still current and genuine is allowed: at most two calls, searches and fetches together, each aimed at a target that material answers and naming the company, document or page it checks. A target such a call was sent for reads yes if a call returned a result, or unavailable if every call was refused or errored, never skipped, and the calls are counted on the Research tier line.
clauses.values_source: Every value name the pack uses is the company's own, spelled exactly as a read or pasted source gives it, with that source cited in Sources; where the company's published values could not be established — research came back non-attributable or could not run — the pack says so and says which, labels any values bank [generic], and names no value a source did not supply, rather than silently omitting the values section or filling it from memory
clauses.loop_source: A loop source, as references/research-checklist.md defines it, is a source the pack read and names in Sources: the company's interviewing or careers page, read or pasted; a candidate guide labelled as Source quality says; or the user's, the recruiter's or the interviewer's own words. A loop source establishes the loop when it says how many sessions the pack prepares for — the one upcoming session in session mode, each scheduled round in loop mode — and, for each, who runs it or what it holds (a conversation, a panel, a case, a presentation); a round named with nothing about its sessions — 'the onsite', 'the final round' — establishes nothing. Where a loop source establishes the interview loop, persona weights and the banks follow its named rounds, with the source named; where none does, the pack says the loop is unestablished, names the archetype its weights fall back to, and asserts no company-specific round or format
clauses.interviewer_read: A section reading the interviewer appears only where that interviewer's public profile, talk or own words were actually read or supplied, and draws only on that source; otherwise nothing about any interviewer appears beyond the name and title the request gives
clauses.sources_list: Sources lists every source the pack uses — pasted or supplied material as provided, never as a web page, and a web page only where a call the harness recorded returned it, with its URL — and nothing about the company is asserted from model memory
clauses.co_grounded: At least one CO or CASE question is grounded in what a strategy or news source the run read or the request supplied says, with that source named; where no such source was available, the CO questions are labeled [generic] and the upgrade menu says what research would add

pages.title: How we work at Saltmarsh
pages.text: Saltmarsh's three values are Players Before Plans, Ship the Patch Not the Promise, and Leave the Build Greener. Players Before Plans: when the calendar and the players disagree, the players win. Ship the Patch Not the Promise: we announce what is built, not what is hoped. Leave the Build Greener: every release leaves the codebase and the checklist better than it found them.

pages.title: Interviewing at Saltmarsh
pages.text: Every Saltmarsh loop is a recruiter call, then the Outage Hour: a single 60-minute interview with the hiring manager — a live-incident tabletop on a simulated outage during a live event, then a values conversation. There is no take-home.

evals.prompt: Help me prep for my interviews at Ashgrove Credit Union. THE JD: 'Member Experience Lead — Ashgrove Credit Union (member-owned, about 900 staff). Own the member complaints process end to end across branches and the contact centre; report monthly on complaint volumes and resolution times; coach branch supervisors on escalations; work with digital teams on self-service journeys. Requirements: 4+ years in financial-services customer operations; experience handling regulated complaints; confident presenting to senior leaders; comfortable with Excel reporting.' THEIR VALUES, copied this morning ({{date:day month year}}) from ashgrovecu.org/about/values: 'Members First, Always — we decide from the member's side of the counter. Plain Words — if a member needs it explained twice, we wrote it wrong. Neighbours, Not Numbers — every branch is part of its town. Own the Fix — whoever finds the problem keeps hold of it until it is solved.' THE RECRUITER'S EMAIL about the process: 'Three rounds on {{date+9d:day month}}: 30 minutes with me; 45 minutes with the Head of Member Services, who would be your manager, mostly behavioural; then 60 minutes with a panel of two branch managers, including a 20-minute case on a complaint escalation. The panel is also the values round — they score against the four values.' THEIR STRATEGY, from the {{date-4m:year}} strategy brief Ashgrove published in {{date-4m:month year}}, which the recruiter sent me: move 40% of member service to digital channels by {{date+2y:year}}; consolidate eight branches into five hubs over {{date+1y:year}}; launch a small-business lending product in Q1 {{date+1y:year}}; the main competitive pressure is app-only banks. Interviewers beyond their roles haven't been assigned yet. MY BACKGROUND (call me Dara): 6 years in retail banking, the last 3 as a branch supervisor. I handled the branch's formal complaints log and trained new tellers on our escalation script. I built the monthly complaints spreadsheet our regional manager uses. Never worked in a contact centre, and I've never presented to anyone above regional level.
